name: Slow Cooker Beef Tips and Gravy over Mashed Potatoes
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Sirloin tips or cubed chuck in a from-scratch pan gravy over potatoes. Enormously popular search term, nothing like it in the catalog (Salisbury Steak and Potato Bowls is a ground beef patty dish). Scales to 14 servings without any change in technique. Confidence: medium on calories. | HARVEST: Mashed potatoes are a serving suggestion; nutrition covers beef and gravy only.
intro_html: Beef tips and gravy is diner food made honestly: cubes of chuck cooked until tender in a from scratch gravy, no packet required. Cornstarch thickens it at the end, which means you control how thick it gets instead of hoping a packet guessed right. Each bowl carries 39 grams of protein and 561 calories for about $3.34.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Beef Broth, 7 cups: ~$2.26. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 32oz cartons.
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper, worcestershire sauce, dijon mustard, paprika): ~$0.21. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $46.81 across 14 servings, so roughly $3.34 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $53.77 across 14 servings, roughly $3.84 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $20.48 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $74.25. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $3.34 a bowl. Seven ingredients, one of which is oil and one of which is cornstarch, so the beef and the broth are essentially the whole cost.
shop_smart: Buy a chuck roast and cube it yourself instead of buying packaged stew meat or beef tips. You will pay less per pound and you will know exactly what cut you got.
Cornstarch is the cheapest thickener there is and a box lasts years. Mix it with cold water before it goes anywhere near the hot pot or you will be picking out lumps.
Beef broth is the backbone of the gravy. Bouillon base in a jar makes a lot of broth for very little money and keeps in the fridge for months.
Only one onion goes in, so the seasoning matters more than usual. Do not skip the paprika, Dijon, and Worcestershire from the pantry list.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck roast into large cubes, pat them dry, and season with salt, black pepper, and paprika.
Sear the cubes in the olive oil in batches over high heat until they have real color, then move them to the slow cooker.
Cook the chopped onion and minced garlic in the same pan until soft, scraping up every browned bit, then add them to the cooker.
Pour in the beef broth along with the Worcestershire sauce and Dijon mustard from the pantry list.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours, until the beef cubes give with no resistance.
Whisk the cornstarch with a little cold water, stir it into the hot liquid, and cook on high 15 to 20 minutes until the gravy thickens and turns glossy.
Cook the rice separately and spoon the beef tips and gravy over it. In a diner it would be mashed potatoes, and if you keep potatoes on hand that works too.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Spoon that weight of beef tips and gravy into each container, then give every one the same weight of rice. Each bowl lands at 561 calories with 39 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from houseofyumm.com, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.

head.description: Slow cooker beef tips and gravy meal prep: cubed chuck roast braised in a from scratch cornstarch gravy over a starch base. 561 calories, 39g protein, about $3.34 per serving.
head.keywords: beef tips and gravy, slow cooker beef tips, brown gravy from scratch, beef bowls, budget meal prep, chuck roast recipes
steps: Cube and season the chuck roast, then sear it in olive oil in batches.
Soften onion and garlic in the pan and add everything to the slow cooker.
Add beef broth, Worcestershire, and Dijon and cook on low 7 to 8 hours.
Whisk cornstarch with cold water, stir it in, and thicken on high 15 to 20 minutes.
Cook the starch base and portion beef and gravy into 14 containers.
